content: 1. To reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke, it is essential to manage high blood pressure, high cholesterol, and diabetes effectively. Lifestyle modifications that can help include reducing stress, consuming a diet low in fat and salt, losing weight if overweight, engaging in regular physical activity, and quitting smoking. 2. To help prevent dementia, it is recommended to keep your mind active through mental exercises such as reading or solving crossword puzzles. 3. To promote healthy bones, lifestyle changes such as increasing weight-bearing exercises, quitting smoking, limiting alcohol consumption, and eating a well-balanced diet rich in calcium and vitamin D are beneficial. 4. If you miss a dose of your medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 5. Store your medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard the product when it is expired or no longer needed. 6. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about the product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about the product and your specific health needs. 7. Estrogens, whether used alone or with another hormone (progestin), have been associated with rare but serious side effects. Discuss the risks and benefits of hormone therapy with your doctor. Estrogens can increase the risk of uterine cancer (endometrial cancer). Taking a progestin as directed by your doctor can help reduce this risk. 8. In postmenopausal women, estrogens, with or without a progestin, may increase the risk of breast or ovarian cancer, stroke, dementia, and serious blood clots. The risk of these side effects may depend on the dose of estrogen and the duration of use. This medication should be used at the lowest effective dose and for the shortest duration necessary. Regularly discuss the use of this medication with your doctor and have periodic check-ups (e.g., every 3 to 6 months) to determine if continued use is necessary. 9. If you are taking this medication long-term, you should undergo regular complete physical exams (e.g., annually) as directed by your doctor. These exams may include lab tests and medical evaluations such as blood pressure checks, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, and Pap smears. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. 10. This medication is a hormone (estrogen) used by women to alleviate symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes and vaginal dryness, which occur due to decreased estrogen production in the body. Certain estrogen products may also be used postmenopause to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis). However, other medications, such as raloxifene or bisphosphonates (e.g., alendronate), may also be effective in preventing bone loss and could be safer alternatives. 11. Before starting this medication, read the patient information leaflet provided by your pharmacist. Take the medication orally, with or without food, as directed by your doctor. If you are using extended-release tablets, do not crush, chew, or dissolve them, as this can release the drug all at once, increasing the risk of side effects. Take the medication regularly to achieve the best results, and try to take it at the same time(s) each day to help you remember. 12. Common side effects may include stomach upset, nausea, vomiting, bloating, breast tenderness, headache, or weight changes. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefit to you outweighs the risk of side effects. Rarely, this medication may cause serious, sometimes fatal, complications from blood clots, such as heart attack, stroke, or clots in the lungs or legs. 13. A severe allergic reaction to this product is rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. 14. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. 15. Avoid smoking or using tobacco while on this medication. Inform your doctor if you have recently undergone or will undergo surgery, or if you will be confined to a chair or bed for an extended period (e.g., during a long flight), as these conditions increase the risk of blood clots, especially when taking estrogen products. 16. This medication may cause blotchy, dark areas on the skin (melasma). Sunlight can worsen this effect, so limit your time in the sun and avoid tanning booths and sunlamps. Use sunscreen and wear protective clothing when outdoors. 17. If you are nearsighted or wear contact lenses, you may experience vision problems or difficulty wearing your lenses while on this medication. 18. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug, which could affect their growth and development. 19. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It passes into breast milk and may reduce the quality and quantity of milk produced. 20. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use (including prescription/nonprescription drugs and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., metyrapone test), potentially causing false results. 21. In case of overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911. Otherwise, contact a poison control center immediately. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. 22. Regular complete physical exams, including lab and/or medical tests (e.g., blood pressure, breast exams/mammograms, pelvic exams, Pap smears), should be conducted while taking this medication. Follow your doctor’s instructions for breast self-exams and report any lumps immediately. Keep all medical and lab appointments.
